FARM-LEVEL SYSTEM

The journey begins at the farm, where milk is produced and collected directly from cows and buffaloes.

KEY FUNCTIONS
  • Animal → milk production
  • Farmer → milking and initial handling
  • Milk → collected into cans
  • Initial quality and handling conditions begin here
SYSTEM ROLE
The farm is the origin point of the entire milk system. The quality and quantity of milk entering the system begin at this stage.
FLOW
Animal → Farmer → Milk → Collection

02 / 06 AGGREGATION & CHILLING

MILK COLLECTION CENTRES

Milk from individual farmers is aggregated at collection points before entering the larger cold-chain network.

KEY FUNCTIONS
  • Milk collection from farmers
  • Quantity measurement
  • Initial quality testing
  • Milk aggregation
  • Chilling / temperature control
  • Transfer to the next stage
SYSTEM ROLE
Collection centres connect dispersed farms to the organized dairy system and help maintain milk quality before transportation.
FLOW
Farmers → Collection → Testing → Chilling → Transport
Logistics • Bulk Milk Transport

MILK TANKER

Insulated road tankers transferring chilled milk from rural BMCs to central dairy plants.

~10,000 L Tankers ~20,000 L Tankers ~45,000 L Bulk Units >80 Tankers / Day

Strict Cold Chain: Departure at ~3–4°C • Arrival at ~6–7°C. Insulated stainless steel barrels preserve freshness.

High-Frequency Transit: ~600 km Chittoor trunk route completed in ~5.5–7 hours with real-time GPS tracking.

Producers • Village Network

FARMERS / SUPPLIERS

Local farmers delivering freshly harvested milk to the village collection centre twice daily.

Farmer ID Gross Quantity FAT % SNF % Quality Grade

Transparent Settlement: Instant digital recording links milk quality and quantity directly to automated bank payments.

Tested → Weighed → Chilled
Quality Control • Ingestion Gate

MILK TESTING & QC

Automated analyzers evaluating milk purity before entry into bulk storage tanks.

Quantity (Kg) FAT Analysis SNF (Solid-Not-Fat) Quality Result

Gatekeeping Integrity: Test data determines milk acceptance, processing segregation, and fair producer payouts.

Infrastructure • Cold Aggregation

BULK MILK COOLER (BMC)

Stainless steel chilling tanks aggregating raw milk from multiple producers.

Chilling Target: ~4°C BMC: 25k–30k L MCC: 1.5 Lakh L Holding: 1–2 Days

Aggregation Buffer: Bridges the gap between small dispersed village collections and bulk 45,000 L tanker transit.

Dependencies & Risks: Continuous electricity • Rapid refrigeration • Power backup • Temp monitoring.

Operations • Facility Staff

COLLECTION & CHILLING STAFF

Operate reception intake, record volumes, execute milk testing, oversee chilling tanks, and coordinate tanker pump loading.

Milk Testers Chilling Operators Procurement Staff Tanker Drivers
First-Mile • Rural Transit

VILLAGE MILK DELIVERY

03 / 06 COLD-CHAIN TRANSIT

TANKERS & ROAD NETWORK

Tankers physically connect the collection network to Sangam Dairy. The road network determines how reliably and quickly milk can move between locations.

KEY FUNCTIONS
  • Chilled milk transportation
  • Tanker capacity management
  • Route planning
  • Distance and travel-time dependency
  • Temperature protection during transit
SYSTEM ROLE
Transport converts geographic distance into a time and temperature dependency.
FLOW
Milk Available → Tanker Capacity → Road Network → Travel Time → Sangam
KEY DEPENDENCY
Road disruption → Travel delay → Longer temperature exposure → Milk-quality risk
Logistics • Physical Carrier

01 — TANKER

Physical carrier that moves collected milk between facilities and Sangam Dairy.

10,000 L 20,000 L ~45,000 L 80+ Tankers / Day

Carries collected & chilled milk under strict temperature requirements during movement.

System Relationship: Milk available → Tanker capacity → Transport → Sangam.

Key Dependency: Milk reaching Sangam depends on available tanker capacity at the right time.

• Vehicle breakdown
• Vehicle capacity limitation
• Refrigeration failure
• Milk leakage / spillage
• Accident
Infrastructure • Road Transit

02 — ROAD NETWORK

The tanker can only move as reliably as the roads allow.

Example Journey ~600 km
Speed 100–120 km/h
Driving Time 5–6 h
With Stops/Tolls ~5.5–7 h

System Relationship: Road condition → Travel time → Milk arrival → Temperature exposure.

Key Insight: Road disruptions do not remain just road problems—they become milk-quality and supply problems.

System Flow • Duration

03 — TIME

For milk transport, distance becomes time.

Transit Dependency: Longer transit increases reliance on:

Reliable Vehicles Reliable Roads Temp Control Timely Arrival

Main Risk: Transport delay (milk takes too long to reach next node).

System Connection: Distance → Travel time → Milk arrival → Temperature exposure.

Time connects the road system directly to the cold-chain system.

Cold Chain • 4°C Protection

04 — TEMPERATURE CONTROL

The tanker is expected to actively protect milk temperature during movement.

Temperature Rise: Milk warms during movement if temperature control is inadequate.

Refrigeration Failure Long Transit Road Delays

System Relationship:
Transport delay → Longer transit → Greater temperature exposure → Temperature rise → Milk quality risk.

Target: Maintained strictly at 4°C.

04 / 06 PLANT INTAKE GATEWAY

RAW MILK RECEIVING DOCK (RMRD)

RMRD is the point where incoming milk officially enters Sangam's plant system.

KEY FUNCTIONS
  • Tanker reception
  • Milk quantity verification
  • Sampling
  • Quality testing
  • Receiving decision
  • Direction into the processing system
SYSTEM ROLE
Milk is not immediately sent into production. It is first received, measured, sampled and assessed before entering the processing system.
FLOW
Tanker → Reception → Weighing → Sampling → Quality Decision → Processing
Factory Gateway • Ingestion Node

RMRD • RAW MILK RECEIVING DOCK

The point where milk enters Sangam's factory system. Arriving milk does not immediately become part of production.

1. RECEIVED • Tanker docking & intake
2. MEASURED • Quantity verification
3. TESTED • Lab quality analysis
4. QUALITY DECISION • Acceptance clearance
5. PROCESSING SYSTEM • Transfer to silos

Gateway Linkage:

EXTERNAL MILK NETWORK → SANGAM DAIRY PROCESSING SYSTEM

Milk must pass through receiving and quality control before entering production.

01 • TANKER RECEPTION

01 — TANKER RECEPTION

Incoming milk reception & volume verification.

Intake Sequence:

• Tanker enters the plant
• Milk quantity is checked (weighbridge)
• Milk is sampled for QC
• Directed into receiving lines
• Quality information recorded

Key Question: “How much milk arrived?”

Key Insight: The quantity received by Sangam is verified rather than simply assuming that the quantity sent from the collection network is the quantity received.

MILK SENT → MILK RECEIVED → QUANTITY VERIFIED
02 • RMRD LAB

02 — RMRD LAB

Quality-control interface at receiving. Supports the quality decision before milk enters the processing system.

MBRT Methylene Blue Reduction Test

Primary Role: Microbiological quality indicator evaluating freshness and bacterial activity.

Quality Gate:

MILK ARRIVES → SAMPLE
→ QUALITY CHECK → QUALITY DECISION
Bulk Processing • Homogeneity

AGITATION / MIXING

Milk is gently circulated / agitated to maintain a uniform composition.

Milk is not simply treated as a static liquid sitting in a tank. Continuous gentle movement keeps milk mixed and uniform before downstream stages.

1. AGITATION • Constant gentle circulation
2. UNIFORM COMPOSITION • Prevents fat separation
3. CONSISTENT DOWNSTREAM PROCESS • Standardized flow

05 / 06 STORAGE BUFFER & LINE

RAW MILK STORAGE → PROCESSING

After receiving and acceptance, milk enters controlled storage before moving through the processing line.

KEY FUNCTIONS
  • Raw milk storage
  • Controlled temperature
  • Agitation / mixing
  • Filtration / clarification
  • Controlled transfer into processing
SYSTEM ROLE
Storage creates a controlled buffer between milk reception and processing while maintaining milk quality and a consistent flow into the next stage.
FLOW
RMRD → Raw Milk Storage → Agitation / Mixing → Clarification → Processing
01 • Intake Node

Milk Reception / Weighing

Starting point of the processing line.

Machine: Large vertical receiving tank immediately after the tanker.

What happens: Milk from the tanker enters the factory and is received into the milk-receiving system.

Visual Flow: Tanker → Large vertical tank.

This is the starting point of the processing line.

02 • Purification

Filtration / Clarification

Removal of physical impurities.

Machine: The pair of tall cylindrical vessels immediately after the receiving tank.

What happens: Physical impurities / foreign particles are removed from the incoming milk.

Process Relationship: Receiving tank → Filtration / clarification vessels.

This stage can be understood as FILTRATION / CLARIFICATION.

Milk Flow
Cream Flow
03 • Stream Division

Separation — Milk + Cream

Centrifugal separation into distinct streams.

Machine: The conical / rounded machine with the motor at the bottom, around the middle-left of the process line.

What happens: Milk → Separator → Milk + Cream. Divides incoming milk into milk and cream.

Dual Stream: The two outlet pipes visually represent the separation into the two streams.

Label: SEPARATION

Pasteurization • 72°C Heat Treatment
04 • Thermal Treatment

4. Pasteurization

Controlled thermal treatment for safety and shelf-life.

Machine: The large rectangular plate-like heat exchanger immediately after the separator.

This is the pasteurization stage.

What happens: Milk is heat-treated and then moved onward through the processing line.

Label: PASTEURIZATION

05 • Emulsification

Homogenization

High-pressure mechanical fat-globule breakdown.

Machine: The smaller compact machine immediately after the pasteurization unit, before the larger cooling equipment.

What happens: The milk is processed under high pressure to reduce fat-globule size and create a more uniform mixture.

Label: HOMOGENIZATION

Chiller Fans Active • 4°C
06 • Cold Stabilization

Cooling / Chilling

Rapid refrigeration to storage temperature.

Machine: The larger rectangular refrigeration / chiller unit with the two circular fans on top.

This is the COOLING / CHILLING stage.

What happens: The milk is cooled/chilled before moving into storage.

Label: COOLING

Chilled Silos • Agitation Active
07 • Final Silos

Milk Storage

Buffer holding prior to packaging and dispatch.

Machines: The two huge cylindrical stainless-steel tanks at the far right.

These are the final milk storage tanks.

Final Stage: Retains processed, chilled milk ready for packaging.

Label: STORAGE

06 SUBSYSTEM

MILK SEPARATION

Explore →
06 / 06 STREAM BIFURCATION

MILK SEPARATION

Processed milk enters the separator, where it is divided into two product streams: milk and cream.

KEY FUNCTIONS
  • Processed milk input
  • Separation
  • Milk stream
  • Cream stream
  • Dedicated storage
  • Controlled downstream flow
SYSTEM ROLE
Separation is the key transition point where one processed milk stream becomes two distinct product streams.
FLOW
PROCESSED MILK ↓ MILK SEPARATOR
↙ MILK
↘ CREAM
PROCESSED MILK →
02 • Centrifuge

Centrifugal Milk Separator

High-speed rotational fraction separation.

Mechanism: Conical centrifuge disc bowl rotating at 5,000–6,000 RPM creates intense gravitational acceleration.

Denser skim milk is forced outward while lighter butterfat cream gathers at the axial center.

Separation Streams: Separates continuous processed milk intake into high-fat CREAM (~40% fat) and standardized/skim MILK.

Piping: Stainless steel lines route cream to the upper tank and milk to the lower tank.

03 • Rich Fraction

Cream Storage Vessel

Separated high-fat fraction buffer holding.

Vessel: Top stainless steel tank holding separated pure cream with gentle low-shear agitation.

Quality Control: Continuous fat percentage monitoring and chilling at 4°C.

Product Destiny: Feeds downstream butter churning, traditional Sangam Ghee processing, and fresh table cream.

Label: CREAM

04 • Main Stream

Standardized Milk Vessel

Clarified and fat-standardized liquid milk.

Vessel: Lower stainless steel tank receiving the clarified milk stream after precision fat separation.

Standardization: Blended to exact regulatory fat/SNF ratios (Toned, Double Toned, Whole Milk).

Next Step: Moves directly to aseptic pouch packing lines and liquid milk distribution network.

Label: MILK

Stage 06 • Centrifugal Stream Separation

↓
MILK SEPARATOR

MILK
CREAM

PROCESSED MILK SILO

Role: Holds processed milk before it enters the separation stage.

  • Receives milk from the previous processing stage.
  • Acts as the input/storage point for the separation process.
  • Feeds milk continuously into the separator through connected piping.
  • Maintains a controlled flow into the separation system.

MILK SEPARATOR

Role: Separates processed milk into MILK and CREAM.

  • Receives processed milk from the silo.
  • Separates the milk into two streams: MILK + CREAM.
  • Connected piping directs each output to its respective storage vessel.
  • Acts as the key transition point between processed milk and the two product streams.

CREAM

Role: Separated cream output from the milk-separation process.

  • Cream is separated from the processed milk.
  • Collected in a dedicated storage vessel.
  • Forms a separate stream for subsequent cream-based processing.

MILK

Role: Main milk stream after separation.

  • Separated from the cream during the separation process.
  • Collected in a dedicated storage vessel.
  • Continues onward for further processing/product manufacturing.

Farm-Level System • Core Dynamics

Core Function

Milk is produced at individual rural farms through dedicated animal care, nutrition feeding, genetic breeding, and morning milking.

Main Actors
Farmers Farm Workers Cows Buffaloes Veterinarians
Key Dependencies
Feed & Fodder Veterinary Support Water Supply Market / Payment System
Crucial System Relationship

Producer Returns → Supply Security: Higher farmer returns provide the incentive for consistent milk production, sustaining overall plant capacity and network trust.

Sangam Milk Producer Collective • Producer-Owned & Farmer-Centric System

BMC / MCC Network • Chilling & Aggregation

Network Structure

~65 BMCs across Andhra Pradesh with one collection node approximately every ~50 km, bridging village milk producers to the central dairy.

Core Capabilities
BMC: 25k–30k L MCC: 1.5 Lakh L Chilling: ~4°C Buffer: 1–2 Days
Key Flow Sequence

Farmers → Village Collection → BMC/MCC → Road Tankers → Central Dairy Plant

System Risks & Dependencies

Critical Dependencies: Chilling capacity, power backup, testing accuracy, and timely tanker turnaround to prevent temperature rise and souring.
